background: This is Dhaula Dam in north India, in the year 2019.
It is a small hydro dam with a crew of about twenty people.
Heavy monsoon rain has washed out the only road and the phone lines are down.
Everyone is here tonight because the dam is in a flood alert and the crew must stay on site.
The victim is Meera Bhatt, the chief engineer. She was strict, fair, and checked everything twice.
At about 9:30 pm the power was cut for a test. Soon after, Meera was found dead at the bottom of the gate stairwell.
Everyone on a dam site knows that no one works in a control room without a signed safety permit.
scenario.case_question: Who killed chief engineer Meera Bhatt, and why?
scenario.setting_summary: A small hydro dam in the hills, cut off by a flood. The chief engineer is dead at the foot of the gate stairs.
scenario.opening_scene: Rain hits the metal roof like gravel. The road is gone and the phones are dead. At 9:30 the lights went out for a power test. When they came back, Meera Bhatt was lying at the bottom of the gate stairwell, not moving. Four of you are still awake. One of you knows exactly how she got there.

truth.summary: Site manager Himanshu faked concrete test reports for money. Meera found the real logs and was going to send them at dawn. He forged a note in her name so the power would be cut at 9:30, asked Nikhil for a permit that emptied the control room, hit Meera with a torque wrench, dragged her to the gate stairs to look like a fall, and hid the wrench in the diesel shed.

timeline.event: Meera opens the real concrete test logs in the site office and tells Himanshu she will send them at dawn.
Himanshu writes a note in Meera's name telling the electrician to cut power at 9:30.
Guest finds the note in the switch box and gets ready to cut power.
Meera uses the radio and tells the district office that Himanshu faked the reports. The office logs it.
Meera's fax of the first log page goes out before the line dies.
Nikhil signs the permit Himanshu asked for. The corridor and control room are cleared of crew.
Guest cuts the power. The site goes dark.
Himanshu hits Meera on the back of the head with a torque wrench in the control room.
Himanshu drags her to the gate stairwell and leaves her at the bottom. His glove tears on the door latch.
Himanshu hides the wrench behind drums in the diesel shed, then goes to the canteen.
Rishabh finds a torn glove piece in the control room doorway and hides it.
Power returns. Nikhil finds the body and shouts for everyone.

truth.method: A blow to the back of the head with a heavy torque wrench, then the body was dragged and left at the stairs to look like a fall.
truth.motive: Meera had proof that Himanshu faked concrete tests and took money. That proof would send him to prison.
truth.ambiguities: Rishabh stole diesel and Guest has a fake licence, so both look guilty of something. Nikhil signed the permit that cleared the room, which can make him look like a helper.

players.public_info: Himanshu runs the dam site and signs off all the work.
players.private_info: I wanted the bonus money, so I approved cheap concrete and signed fake test reports. Tonight Meera showed me the real logs and said she would send them at dawn. I would lose everything, so I wrote a note in her name to cut the power at 9:30, and I asked Nikhil for a permit to clear the control room. In the dark I hit Meera with a torque wrench, dragged her to the gate stairs, and hid the wrench behind the drums in the diesel shed. My left work glove tore on the door latch and I have not found the piece.
players.wants: I want this night to end with everyone calling Meera's death a fall. I have a wife and a loan and no other way out.
players.fears: I am scared someone finds the real test logs with my signature next to them.
players.goal: Avoid being named as the killer in the final vote.
players.goal_why: If they name me I go to prison and my family loses the house.
players.side_explanation: Himanshu killed Meera Bhatt to stop her proof reaching the district office.

hidden_facts.fact: Meera's fax of the first log page went out at 9:20, before the line died.
Meera named you on the radio at 9:15, and the district office wrote it in their log.

players.starting_knowledge: You know Nikhil signed your permit, you know Guest cut the power because of your note, and you know the wrench is in the diesel shed. You went to the canteen at about 9:45 with wet sleeves and asked Lakshmi for tea. Meera showed you the real test logs in the site office at about 8:30.
players.intro_line: I am Himanshu Rawat, the site project manager. I was in the canteen when the lights came back.
reasons: You signed fake test reports because the bonus money was the only way to clear your loan.
You wrote the note in Meera's name because a dark site gave you cover.
You asked Nikhil for the permit because you needed the control room empty.
You hit Meera because her logs would have sent you to prison.
You dragged her to the stairs because a fall looks like nobody's fault.
You hid the wrench behind the drums because the shed is dark and nobody counts drums.
You went to the canteen for tea because being seen there made you look normal.

night.doing: Waiting and worrying after Meera showed you the logs.
Checking the permit cleared the corridor.
Standing in the dark, waiting for Meera.
Hiding the wrench behind the fuel drums.
Drinking tea when the shouting starts.

players.public_info: Nikhil checks the safety permits and he found Meera's body.
players.private_info: I trusted Meera more than anyone on this site. She asked me to send concrete samples to an outside lab, which breaks company rules, and I did it for her. Tonight Himanshu asked me for a permit to clear the control room at 9:28 and I signed it without asking why. At 10:00 I walked to the stairwell and found Meera dead. I also know Rishabh has been selling site diesel, because I saw him load cans into a jeep last month.
players.wants: I want the truth written down properly, because Meera taught me that paper is how you stop lies. I also want to stay out of jail for the lab samples.
players.fears: I am scared the group learns I broke the rules and stops believing a word I say.
players.goal: Show the group the signed 9:28 permit page before the final vote.
players.goal_why: If that page stays hidden, the man who used my signature walks free.
players.side_explanation: Nikhil wants the killer found and his own rule breaking kept small.

hidden_facts.fact: The permit you signed is what emptied the corridor so Meera could be killed alone.

players.starting_knowledge: You know you signed Himanshu's permit at 9:28, you know you sent Meera's samples out, and you know about Rishabh's diesel. You were walking around the site during the dark half hour.
players.intro_line: I am Nikhil Sharma, the safety inspector. I found Meera at the bottom of the stairs.
reasons: You sent Meera's samples to an outside lab because you trusted her more than the rules.
You signed Himanshu's permit without asking because he is your boss and you were in a hurry.
You walked around in the dark because you were checking the site was safe.
You went to the stairwell at ten because you wanted to check the gates after the test.
You kept quiet about Rishabh's diesel because you felt sorry for his father.

night.doing: Doing paperwork before the test.
Signing the permit Himanshu asked for.
Walking the site in the dark with a torch.
Still walking around, waiting for the power.
Finding Meera's body and shouting for help.

players.public_info: Rishabh keeps the store, the fuel and the radio log.
players.private_info: My father's hospital bills are huge, so I have been selling site diesel and faking the ledger. Tonight at 9:50 I went to the control room and found a torn piece of a rubber glove by the door. I kept it in my pocket because people with secrets do not hand things to inspectors. I also heard Meera on the radio at 9:15 saying someone faked the test reports, but the noise cut her words.
players.wants: I want to keep my job and my father's treatment going, so the diesel ledger must stay closed. I also want the killer caught, because Meera was kind to me.
players.fears: I am scared the group opens the diesel ledger and calls me a thief in front of everyone.
players.goal: Keep the diesel ledger out of the group's hands until the final vote.
players.goal_why: If the theft comes out, my father loses his treatment money.
players.side_explanation: Rishabh wants the killer named without his own stealing coming out.

hidden_facts.fact: Meera had already written a letter asking the company to forgive your diesel debt.

players.starting_knowledge: You know you took the diesel, you know you hid the torn glove piece, and you know Meera's 9:15 radio call.
players.intro_line: I am Rishabh Negi. I run the store and the radio room.
reasons: You sold site diesel because the hospital bills were bigger than your pay.
You faked the ledger so the store count would still look right.
You went to the control room at 9:50 because you wanted to see what happened in the dark.
You pocketed the torn glove piece because a thief does not hand things to inspectors.
You stayed near the radio because you heard Meera's call and it worried you.

night.doing: Hearing Meera on the radio say someone faked reports.
Working on the store ledger.
Sitting in the dark when the power goes.
Leaving the store to walk to the control room.
Holding the torn glove piece in your pocket.

players.public_info: Guest handles the switch room and cut the power for the 9:30 test.
players.private_info: I came here with a licence page I paid for, because my real exam result never came. Tonight I found a note in the switch box signed with Meera's initials, telling me to cut power at 9:30, so I did it. The dark lasted thirty minutes and I sat alone by the switches. Now a woman is dead and my hand is on the switch that made the dark.
players.wants: I want my fake licence page out of the office file and burned, so I can keep working and feeding my mother. I also want to know who used me.
players.fears: I am scared they check my licence and send me home with nothing.
players.goal: Take the fake licence page from the office file and burn it before the final vote.
players.goal_why: That one page is the only thing standing between my mother and no income.
players.side_explanation: Guest cares more about destroying her licence page than about who gets named.

hidden_facts.fact: The note telling you to cut power was written by Himanshu, not Meera.

players.starting_knowledge: You know you cut the power at 9:30, you know the note told you to, and you know your licence page is in the office file.
players.intro_line: I am Guest Dsouza, the night electrician. I cut the power at 9:30 for the test.
reasons: You bought the licence page because your real exam result never came and you needed work.
You cut the power at 9:30 because the note carried Meera's initials and orders are orders.
You stayed by the switches in the dark because that is where an electrician must be.
You want the page burned because a check of the file would end your job.

night.doing: Getting the switch box ready for the test.
Standing by the switches with the note in hand.
Cutting the power.
Sitting alone by the switches in the dark.
Putting the power back on.

npcs.name: Bahadur Thapa
npcs.public_info: Bahadur sits at the gate hut all night with a flask of tea.
npcs.knows: He knows the road is washed out and nobody came in or left after 7 pm.
npcs.lies: He says he was awake all night, though he dozed for a while.
npcs.reveals_freely: No vehicle moved after 7 pm, and the only way out is blocked.
npcs.reveals_under_pressure: He admits he slept a little and tells people to ask Nikhil, who was walking about.

npcs.name: Lakshmi Devi
npcs.public_info: Lakshmi cooks for the crew and keeps the canteen open late.
npcs.knows: She knows who ate late and who came in wet.
npcs.lies: She says she never gossips, which is not true.
npcs.reveals_freely: Who was in the canteen after the lights came back.
npcs.reveals_under_pressure: She says Himanshu came in at about 9:45 with wet sleeves and asked for tea.

clues.name: Torque wrench behind the drums
clues.shows: A heavy wrench with blood and hair on it is hidden behind the fuel drums.
clues.does_not_prove: It does not show whose hand held it.

clues.name: The body's injuries
clues.shows: Meera has one deep wound on the back of her head and no other bruises.
clues.does_not_prove: It does not say which tool made the wound.

clues.name: Real concrete test logs
clues.shows: The true test results in Meera's drawer say the concrete failed badly.
clues.does_not_prove: It does not say who faked the reports.

clues.name: Signed fake test report
clues.shows: A clean test report with good numbers carries Himanshu's signature.
clues.does_not_prove: It does not prove he knew the numbers were false.

clues.name: Note from the switch box
clues.shows: A note signed M.B. orders the 9:30 power cut, but the handwriting is not Meera's.
clues.does_not_prove: The note alone does not name the writer.

clues.name: Permit book page
clues.shows: The 9:28 permit clearing the control room was requested by Himanshu and signed by Nikhil.
clues.does_not_prove: It does not prove Nikhil knew why the room had to be empty.

clues.name: Torn glove piece
clues.shows: A torn bit of rubber glove from the control room door matches the empty left glove in Himanshu's locker.
clues.does_not_prove: It does not show when the glove tore.

clues.name: Diesel ledger gap
clues.shows: Four hundred litres of diesel are missing from the store ledger.
clues.does_not_prove: It has nothing to do with Meera's death.

clues.name: Radio and fax log
clues.shows: At 9:15 Meera told the district office that Himanshu faked the reports, and a fax went out at 9:20.
clues.does_not_prove: It does not prove she was killed for it.

clues.name: Drag marks and boot prints
clues.shows: Wet drag marks run from the control room door to the top of the stairs.
clues.does_not_prove: The prints are too smeared to match one pair of boots.

clues.name: Meera's unsent letter
clues.shows: Meera wrote to the company asking them to forgive Rishabh's diesel debt, in her own clear handwriting.
clues.does_not_prove: It does not clear Rishabh of stealing.

clues.name: Guest's licence page
clues.shows: Guest's licence page in the staff file is a fake.
clues.does_not_prove: It does not link Guest to Meera's death.

key_deductions.statement: Meera did not fall. Someone hit her on the head with a heavy tool.
She was killed in the control room and then dragged to the stairs.
The 9:30 power cut and the empty room were arranged by Himanshu, not by Meera.
Himanshu faked the concrete reports and Meera had the proof.
Himanshu is the killer: his glove, his note, and his hiding place.

A safety permit clears the control room corridor.
The power is cut for a test. The site goes dark.
Himanshu arrives in the canteen with wet sleeves and asks for tea.
The power returns and Nikhil finds Meera dead at the stairs.

try: Look at the wound on her head.
Ask Lakshmi who came in wet.
phases.planned_beat: Rain gets into the stairwell and starts washing the drag marks away. The group must look now.
phases.question: How did Meera die?
options: She fell down the wet stairs
She was hit on the head with a heavy tool
She was shocked by live wires
She drowned in the gate pit
phases.reward: The group learns the drag marks start at the control room door.
phases.wrong_nudge: A fall breaks arms and legs too. Her arms are clean. Look again at the wound.

hint_ladder.text: Stop asking who was in the dark. Ask who made the dark happen.
Two pieces of paper tonight are signed in Meera's name but not in her hand.
Compare the switch box note with Meera's unsent letter in the office drawer.
Someone is carrying a torn piece of rubber glove in their pocket.
Open every locker. One pair of work gloves is missing its left glove.

twists.name: The unknowing helper

key_times.what: Meera uses the radio in the control room.
A safety permit clears the control room corridor.

Himanshu comes into the canteen with wet sleeves.
The power returns and Meera is found dead.

events.text: Rain hits the metal roof like gravel. The road is gone and the phones are dead. At 9:30 the lights went out for a power test. When they came back, Meera Bhatt was lying at the bottom of the gate stairwell, not moving. Four of you are still awake. One of you knows exactly how she got there.
Round 1 of 3: The Body at the Stairs

events.q: Stairs were wet in that rain right, anyone actually checked if she slipped from the top step?
events.text: Nobody has checked the top step yet. The stairs are wet steel, so a slip is possible. Nikhil found the body, so ask him what he saw, and go look at the top step and the handrail for scuff marks.

read.attempt: Himanshu Rawat asks whether anyone checked if she slipped from the top step of the stairs.
read.said_aloud: Stairs were wet in that rain right, anyone actually checked if she slipped from the top step?

events.text: Rishabh kneels by the body and points at drag marks on the stairs.
Nikhil shows a clue. Torque wrench behind the drums: A heavy wrench with blood and hair on it is hidden behind the fuel drums.

events.q: Drag marks could be from Nikhil pulling her to check breathing right? Nikhil, did you move her at all?
events.text: Only Nikhil can answer that, so he has to say it himself. But the drag marks run up several steps, not just beside the body. And the bloody wrench was hidden behind the fuel drums, far from the stairs.

Time to vote: How did Meera die?
The group picked: She was hit on the head with a heavy tool. That is right! The group learns the drag marks start at the control room door.
Round 2 of 3: Thirty Minutes of Dark
The drag marks begin at the control room door. Inside, the permit book lies open and a note signed M.B. sits in the switch box. Lakshmi says someone burned paper in her drain tonight.

Where we are now. Meera was hit on the head. She did not fall down the stairs. Nikhil found a bloody wrench hidden behind the fuel drums. The drag marks start at the control room door, not the top step. Lakshmi says someone burned a paper in the canteen drain.
New on the timeline: 9:28 pm, A safety permit clears the control room corridor.
This round, your job: Find out who ordered the power cut and who cleared the control room.
This round's goal: Why was the control room empty at 9:30?
Nikhil, the story turns to you.

events.q: Who wrote the note in the switch box? Also, show me your handwriting — all of you, right now.
events.text: Nobody knows yet who wrote it. The note is signed M.B., but a signature can be copied. Compare it with Meera's real writing in the permit book, or in her desk in the site office. Each person decides for themselves whether to show you their handwriting.

read.attempt: Guest Dsouza asks who wrote the note in the switch box and demands everyone show their handwriting.
read.said_aloud: Who wrote the note in the switch box? Also, show me your handwriting — all of you, right now.

events.q: Who signed the 9:28 permit in the control room book, and who asked for it?
events.text: The permit book is lying open in the control room. The board says Nikhil was there at 9:28, signing the permit. Who asked for it is still unknown, so read the request line in the book and ask Himanshu, since he signs off all work.

read.attempt: Rishabh Negi asks who signed the 9:28 permit in the control room book and who asked for it.
read.said_aloud: Who signed the 9:28 permit in the control room book, and who asked for it?

events.q: Guest was burning a paper in the canteen drain at 9:45. What was it, and who gave you the switch box note?
events.text: Nobody saw who burned the paper. Lakshmi only smelled burning in the drain, she did not name anyone, and the board puts Guest at the switches. Only Guest can say where the note came from, so dig in the drain for scraps and ask Lakshmi who walked past her kitchen.

read.attempt: Himanshu Rawat asks the room what Guest was burning and who gave him the switch box note.
read.said_aloud: Guest was burning a paper in the canteen drain at 9:45. What was it, and who gave you the switch box note?

events.q: Nikhil, who asked you to sign the 9:28 permit? And did anyone hand you a folded note that night?
events.text: Only Nikhil can answer that, so he has to say it himself. The permit book is open in the control room and has a request line. Read that line out loud, and check if the writing matches the note in the switch box.

read.attempt: Guest Dsouza asks Nikhil who asked him to sign the 9:28 permit and if anyone handed him a folded note that night.
read.said_aloud: Nikhil, who asked you to sign the 9:28 permit? And did anyone hand you a folded note that night?

events.q: Nikhil, who asked you for that 9:28 permit? And whose locker has a left glove with no pair?
events.text: Only Nikhil can say who asked him for that permit, so he has to answer it himself. Nobody has reported a stray left glove, and no lockers have been searched yet. Go open the lockers in the store shed, and ask Bahadur who walked toward the control room before 9:28.

read.attempt: Rishabh Negi asks Nikhil who requested the 9:28 permit and whose locker contains an unpaired left glove.
read.said_aloud: Nikhil, who asked you for that 9:28 permit? And whose locker has a left glove with no pair?

The group picked: Himanshu asked for a permit and Nikhil signed it. That is right! The group learns the switch box note is a forgery in Himanshu's handwriting.

Round 3 of 3: What the Fax Carried

The radio in the control room crackles once. The district office asks about Meera's fax sent at 9:20, and wants the rest of the pages. Nobody here has opened her desk drawer yet. The note in the switch box is in Himanshu's handwriting.

Where we are now. The note that ordered the 9:30 power cut is in Himanshu's handwriting. The 9:28 permit page says Himanshu asked for it and Nikhil signed it. Bahadur saw Himanshu come into the control room alone and stand over that book. The district office says Meera faxed something out at 9:20.
New on the timeline: 10:20 pm, The district office radio crackles once and asks about a fax from Meera.
This round, your job: Find out what Meera was sending at dawn, and who it would ruin.
This round's goal: What did Meera plan to send at dawn?

events.text: Only Himanshu can answer that, so he has to say it himself. Here is a plain fact for the room: Meera faxed something at 9:20, and the power died at 9:30. The fax machine in the site office needs power, and her desk drawer is still unopened.

events.text: Nobody has read the fax page yet. The radio log says Meera told the district office that Himanshu faked the reports, and the fake clean report carries Himanshu's signature. Meera's desk drawer in the site office is still unopened, so open it and read the rest of the pages.

p1.text: In the canteen you see the electrician crouched at the floor drain. A small flame, then burnt paper. Lakshmi asks her what she is burning.

Lakshmi fills your cup and leans close, Himanshu.
Lakshmi Devi: They are all going to the control room now.
Lakshmi Devi: The inspector keeps talking about some permit book.
You think of your locker. Your left work glove is not there.
The rain is still loud. Nobody is watching you yet.

Before the others get to the control room I slip in ahead of them, check the door latch for anything of mine caught on it, and quietly pocket whatever torn cloth is there. Then I stand by the permit book like I am just reading it.

You fold both inside your jacket and press your arm down.
The drawer is lighter than it should be. A letter is missing.
Someone opened this drawer before you tonight.
Voices come up the corridor. You push the drawer shut and step away.

You walk down to the shed and shine the torch behind the fuel drums.
A heavy torque wrench lies on the floor, pushed deep into the gap.
There is dried blood on the heavy end, and two grey hairs stuck in it.
Nobody saw you pick it up. The rain is loud on the shed roof.

p1.how: Himanshu Rawat wrote a note in Meera's name so Guest cut the power at 9:30, and got Nikhil to sign a 9:28 permit clearing the control room. In the dark he hit Meera with a torque wrench, dragged her to the gate stairs, hid the wrench behind the diesel drums, then went to the canteen at 9:45 for tea with wet sleeves. His left glove tore on the door latch.
p1.why: He had approved cheap concrete and signed fake test reports for the bonus. At 8:30 Meera showed him the real logs and said she would send them at dawn, so he killed her to stop the proof reaching the district office.
p1.goal: Not met. My goal was to avoid being named, but the note in my handwriting, the 9:28 permit page, the fax log and the fake report with my signature all pointed at me, and the room ended up on my name.

In the darkness, he hit Meera with a torque wrench, dragged her to the gate stairs, and hid the wrench behind the diesel drums. He went to the canteen at 9:45 for tea with wet sleeves. His left glove tore on the door latch.
read.why: Himanshu had approved cheap concrete and signed fake test reports to obtain a bonus. At 8:30, Meera showed him the real logs and said she would send them to the district office at dawn. He killed her to prevent the proof from reaching the district office.

Note in handwriting pointed at him

p2.how: Himanshu wrote the note ordering the 9:30 power cut and got me to sign a permit clearing the control room at 9:28. In the dark he met Meera at the gate stairwell and hit her once on the back of the head with a torque wrench, then hid it behind the fuel drums in the diesel shed. result.reveal_story:
Here is what really happened at Dhaula Dam.

Himanshu Rawat approved cheap concrete and signed fake test reports for bonus money. At 8:30 Meera Bhatt showed him the real logs and said she would send them at dawn. At 8:50 he wrote a note in her name and left it in the switch box. At 9:15 Meera radioed the district office and named him. At 9:20 one log page faxed out. At 9:28 he asked Nikhil for a permit, and the corridor emptied. At 9:30 Guest cut the power, just as the note told her. At 9:33 Himanshu hit Meera with a torque wrench in the control room. He dragged her to the stairs to look like a fall, hid the wrench behind the fuel drums, and drank tea in the canteen.

Nikhil signed that permit without asking why. Rishabh was selling diesel. Guest's licence was bought. Only Himanshu was a killer.

players.goal_outcome: All four players named him in the final vote, so he failed to escape the blame.
players.comment: You ran a busy, bold cover up, but the burning paper story was too loud to work.
players.coaching: Your best work was chasing your own goal. Next time build one calm alibi instead of accusing many people.

players.goal_outcome: He said the 9:28 permit and Himanshu's request out loud in round 2, and the group accepted it.
players.comment: You found the wrench, the logs and the fax slip, which gave the whole room its backbone.
players.coaching: You are a strong searcher. Next time keep every move inside the story, and remember she was killed in the control room, not at the stairs.

players.goal_outcome: He hid the diesel ledger under the cement sacks and nobody opened it before the vote.
players.comment: You read the body, the drag marks and the drawer, and still kept your own secret buried.
players.coaching: You are excellent at searching. Next time share the glove piece earlier so you look honest too.

players.goal_outcome: She stole her licence page and burned it in the canteen drain, so nobody could check it.
players.comment: You turned being used into an attack, and your question about the exact minute landed hard.
players.coaching: You are sharp at questioning. Next time burn things quietly, because the smell nearly cost you everything.
